title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: October 24, 2026
headline: Sirianni gave no injury clarity on DeVonta Smith's hamstring but praised Eli Stowers' practice week and Makai Lemon's playmaking; Tanner McKee has moved up to No. 2 QB behind Jalen Hurts.
summary: Sirianni said rookie TE Eli Stowers had a good practice week and looked fast and athletic, though he stopped short of saying how that will translate to game usage. He described the bye-week self-scouting as an ongoing process, with an extra day helping the staff review things. He called Marquise Brown (the "Hollywood" reporters referenced, which is an inference) a great professional who made a standout practice catch and will add speed. On Makai Lemon, he said the staff wants to get him the football, that he is a playmaker with phenomenal hands, and that the game plan will determine how he is used. He said DeVonta Smith's hamstring has been a problem since summer, that he is one of the hardest-working players, and that the staff will see where he is. Tanner McKee rose to the No. 2 QB spot through growing comfort in the system and developmental reps, and he stayed committed through the change. On backups, Sirianni said the staff is still learning about the other backup quarterbacks, who are getting scout-team and developmental reps. The Cowboys are the opponent in the Monday Night Football game.

topics.detail: Sirianni said the bye week and the extra day allowed productive self-scouting, and that the staff has adjusted schemes, schedules, and practice in ways he would not detail.
Sirianni compared the NFL's parity to college, emphasized the marathon nature of the season, and said young players must adapt to tighter coverage and contested catches.
The staff is still evaluating the backup quarterbacks, who are getting scout-team and developmental reps. Sirianni did not name a clear order beyond McKee at No. 2.
